::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 5th 1877  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection C0171: Box 29
:::

My dear [Miss Medhurst](people/person_988.qmd)

It is ungrateful not to have thanked you sooner but your letter came while I was from home and I have since been working through the accumulation of things that had arisen on me

What a good photograph yours is. I am sure they are much improved since there was only a little face on the top of a great crinoline. I am afraid the Infirmaries in many places - as well as her own friends will long miss [Miss Mackenzie](people/person_930.qmd).

Thank you for all your kindness to [Emmeline](people/person_1358.qmd).[^1] [Her brother](people/person_2287.qmd) brought his pretty [little boy](people/person_2311.qmd) here for Whitsuntide and I suppose she will appear some time in the summer for her holiday and then I shall hear of you.

I am afraid I must return your verses as they do not quite approve themselves to me

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Medhurst, who occasionally contributed to *MP* and did good works in London, had befriended Emmeline Spratt, the niece of CMY's maid Harriet Spratt.
